topIssues.title: op-core/superchain is unconsumable by downstream Go modules: superchain-configs.zip is gitignored
topIssues.author: jefr90
topIssues.body:
`op-core/superchain` embeds `superchain-configs.zip`, which is gitignored and generated locally from the superchain-registry submodule. The zip is therefore absent from the published Go module, and any downstream module that reaches this package fails to compile:

```
op-core/superchain/chain.go:21:12: pattern superchain-configs.zip: no matching files found
```

### Verification

- The zip is gitignored at every release tag checked: `op-node/v1.17.0`, `v1.18.0`, `v1.19.0`, `v1.19.5`, `op-contracts/v7.0.0`, `op-contracts/v8.0.0-rc.3`. Only `superchain-configs.zip.sha256` is committed.
- The published module confirms it. `$GOMODCACHE/github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism@v1.19.5/op-core/superchain/` contains `superchain-configs.zip.sha256` but no `superchain-configs.zip`.
- `op-core/superchain/sync-superchain.sh` documents three modes (verify, refresh, external). All three require a superchain-registry checkout, so none is usable by a module consumer. There is no consumer-facing README.

The monorepo does not hit this itself because `just build-superchain-go` runs as a build prerequisite, and container builds carry `melange/pipelines/op-stack-go/sync-superchain.yaml`, whose comment documents this exact failure. Neither helps a downstream `go build`.

### Impact

Every OP Stack release from 2026-04-29 onward, when `op-core/superchain` was introduced in #20314, is unconsumable as a plain Go dependency by anything that reaches this package.

Found while upgrading `ethereum-optimism/supersim`, which reaches it via `genesis/worldgen` -> `op-chain-ops/interopgen` -> `op-core/superchain`. supersim had to pin `op-node/v1.16.13` (2026-04-21), the last release before the change, instead of the current one. See ethereum-optimism/supersim#424.

### Possible directions

1. Commit the zip. Simplest, at the cost of a binary in the tree.
2. Make the embed optional behind a build tag, with a runtime loader as the fallback for consumers that do not need the built-in configs.
3. Publish the bundle as a separate versioned Go module or artifact that consumers can depend on.

Happy to take direction on which is preferred.

topIssues.title: flaky test: `TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer`
topIssues.author: geoknee
topIssues.body:
**Claude:** Confirmed flake — failed once, then passed on a rerun of the identical commit with no code change.

**Test:** `TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer`
**File:** `op-acceptance-tests/tests/base/conductor/leadership_transfer_test.go`
**Job:** `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka`

## Occurrences

| When | Job | Branch | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2026-09-17 11:03 UTC | [5574188](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5574188) | `gk/lagoon-span-batch-client-rules` (#22922) | **fail** — 1 of 245 acceptance tests |
| 2026-09-17 (rerun, same commit) | [5574386](https://circleci.com/gh/ethereum-optimism/optimism/5574386) | same | pass |

Encountered while working on #22922, whose diff touches only op-node span-batch decode and the kona protocol crate and cannot reach op-conductor.

## Failure output

```
raft_logger.go:27:  WARN [09-17|11:14:43.296] heartbeat timeout reached, starting election
                         component=conductor name=sequencer chain=901 component=raft
                         last-leader-addr= last-leader-id=

raft.go:290:        ERROR[09-17|11:14:49.161] failed to transfer leadership to server
                         component=conductor name=sequencer chain=901 id=b
                         addr=127.0.0.1:36039 err="leadership transfer timeout"

    Error Trace:  /home/circleci/project/op-devstack/dsl/conductor.go:386
    Error:        Received unexpected error:
                  leadership transfer timeout
    Test:         TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer

--- FAIL: TestLeadershipTransferMovesActiveSequencer (12.55s)
```

## Likely cause

The two log lines are ~6 seconds apart and look causally linked: raft loses its leader (`heartbeat timeout reached, starting election`, with `last-leader-addr=` and `last-leader-id=` both empty), and the explicit `TransferLeader` the test then issues times out because the cluster is mid-election with no leader to transfer *from*.

If that reading is right, this is a raft timing race rather than a product bug: the test asks for a leadership transfer without first establishing that a stable leader exists, so a heartbeat timeout landing in the wrong place fails it. The fix would be to wait for a settled leader before requesting the transfer, and/or to retry the transfer when it returns `leadership transfer timeout`, rather than to lengthen the timeout.

## How often

Rare — as far as I can measure, this is the **first recorded occurrence**:

- Walked the 300 most recent CircleCI pipelines, inspected all 37 failed `memory-all*` jobs and grepped their logs: exactly 1 hit, the one above.
- CircleCI insights for `memory-all-opn-op-reth-fusaka` on `develop`: 5 failures in 217 runs (97.7%) over 2026-08-11 → 2026-09-16, but the most-failed-tests window (100 runs) does not list this test, and the flaky-tests endpoint records a different test for this job (`TestInteropFilter_IngressRejectsInvalid`).
- No pre-existing issue matches the test name.

Filing it anyway so the next occurrence lands somewhere rather than being rediscovered.

## Possibly related

`TestSequencerFailover_DisasterRecovery_OverrideLeader` — 1/62 failures in `go-tests` per CircleCI insights. Different test, same conductor-leadership area, and plausibly the same underlying raft-timing sensitivity. Worth checking together if anyone picks this up.

topPRs.title: Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested)
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Silhouette: private interoperable chains (v1, attested) A silhouette chain is a private L2 that participates in an ordinary interop dependency set. Its transactions stay private. L1 carries a signed proof envelope describing the chain's public outline and a standard derivation carrier with user transactions removed. v1 is explicitly operator-attested: the trusted submitter's L1 signature authenticates the claimed state. The wire reserves a proof slot for a future proven mode, but this PR contains no ZK toolchain or L1 settlement path. ### Architecture - **No `op-node` changes.** The final PR diff under `op-node/` is empty. - **No custom submitter.** The normal `op-batcher` loads real private blocks, receipts and output roots and retains its normal channel, reorg, txmgr and retry lifecycle. A terminal encoder emits the silhouette proof envelope followed by standard carrier frames for the same block cadence with user transactions removed. - **Normal inbox and stock portal.** Both envelope and carrier go to the rollup's normal batch inbox. Deposits remain enabled and are stock-derived; there is no gated portal contract. - **Stock derivation.** A stock verifier `op-node` ignores the `KCPB` proof blob as an unknown derivation format, consumes the following standard carrier frames, and runs the ordinary Holocene/interop rewind and deposits-only replacement path. - **One verifier-only supernode role.** Silhouette chains cannot be sequenced by a supernode virtual node. Private sequencing is performed by a LightCL op-node backed by the private EL. - **Standalone magic EL.** `op-silhouette-el` is an in-memory Engine/eth RPC service. It watches the authenticated proof stream independently, maps stock carrier attributes to proof-committed block hashes and roots, and delegates a stock deposits-only replacement build to the private EL when interop invalidates a proven block. - **Normal interop semantics.** The supernode's stock judge validates the private chain's declared imports against independently derived public-chain messages. Invalid blocks are replaced and transitive invalidation propagates across chains. ### What is posted to L1 Each normal batcher submission contains: 1. `KCPB` envelope magic, wire version, public-values length/data, and proof length/data (empty in attested mode). 2. Batch commitments: previous/new output root, L1 head hash, rollup-config hash, dependency-set hash, export-policy hash, and the block list. 3. Per block: number, timestamp, real block hash, state root, message-passer storage root, exported logs, imported messages, L1-origin hash/number, and sequence number. 4. Per exported log: real block log index, log hash, and optional preimage (empty under the default all-hashes policy). 5. Per imported message: origin, source block/log index/timestamp/chain ID, and payload hash. 6. Standard compressed derivation channel/frame data carrying each block's parent, epoch, timestamp, stock deposits/L1-info transaction, and an empty user-transaction list. It does **not** publish private user transaction bytes or hashes, senders, calldata, receipts, contract state, or full log contents. The ordinary L1 blob transaction still exposes its sender, destination inbox, nonce, fees, commitments and inclusion block. ### Images Build these three branch-specific targets: ```sh docker buildx bake op-batcher op-supernode op-silhouette-el ``` | Image | Difference from a normal interop deployment | |---|---| | `op-batcher` | Enables the terminal silhouette proof + stripped-carrier encoding. | | `op-supernode` | Loads the silhouette verifier manifest and proof observer. It remains verifier-only. | | `op-silhouette-el` | New in-memory proof-backed Engine/eth service used as P's verifier EL. | The standalone `op-node`, L1/L2 execution clients, and portal contracts are stock. There is no `proofbatch-submitter` image. ### Minimal configuration delta Private producer: ```sh op-batcher --data-availability-type blobs --silhouette \ --max-pending-tx 1 --target-num-frames 6 \ --silhouette.inbox $NORMAL_BATCH_INBOX --silhouette.wire-version 4 \ --silhouette.rollup-config-hash $ROLLUP_HASH \ --silhouette.dependency-set-hash $DEPSET_HASH ``` The producer is otherwise a normal LightCL sequencer + private EL. It uses the stock `OptimismPortal`; the silhouette inbox must equal the normal rollup batch inbox. Magic EL: ```sh op-silhouette-el --l1 $L1_RPC --l1.beacon $L1_BEACON \ --supernode $SUPERNODE_RPC --rollup-config rollup-p.json \ --verifier-config verifier-p.json \ --replacement-engine $PRIVATE_ENGINE_AUTH_RPC \ --replacement-engine.jwt-secret jwt.txt --rpc.addr 0.0.0.0 --rpc.port 9545 ``` Verifier supernode: ```sh op-supernode --silhouette manifest.json \ --vn.

.l2 http://op-silhouette-el:9545 \ --vn.

.interop.dependency-set depset.json ``` The `op-node` VN has no silhouette/private flag: its only unusual input is that its configured EL endpoint speaks the proof-backed Engine API. The manifest names P's verifier config; A is absent and remains an ordinary chain. The verifier config binds L1 chain ID, trusted submitter, normal inbox, rollup/dependency-set hashes, `proofType: "attested"`, `wireVersion: 4`, and the anchor. ### Local network and smoke tests ```sh go run ./op-up --silhouette # funded transactional RPCs: A http://127.0.0.1:8545, B http://127.0.0.1:8546 go run ./op-up smoke-interop all go run ./op-up smoke-interop invalid-message --direction both --reorg-timeout 5m go run ./op-up smoke-interop chained-invalid-message --require-cascade --reorg-timeout 5m # comparison topology go run ./op-up --interop ``` Observed locally on this revision: - silhouette `smoke-interop all`: PASS; - bidirectional invalid A→B and B→A: both replaced and both chains resumed; - strict chained invalidation: invalid P block, direct dependent, and descendant dependent all reorged while the independent control remained; - normal sysgo bidirectional invalid smoke: same replacement/resume semantics (lower latency because it does not wait for the proof-batch cadence); - focused `TestSilhouetteImportThatIsFalseIsReplaced`: PASS; - `op-batcher`, all `op-supernode`, sysgo/presets, smoke utility, and `op-up` unit suites: PASS. The serialized full silhouette acceptance package still has one known timeout in `TestSilhouetteCrossChainPinsThenAdvances`; the replacement regression and proof-slot refusal tests pass independently. ### Diff size Against the PR base: approximately **24.3k insertions / 1.45k deletions across 267 files**. Much of the file count is the existing cross-language fixture corpus. The architecture rewrite in the latest commit is **3,487 insertions / 7,004 deletions**: it deletes the custom submitter, sequencing-side silhouette role, custom portal, and op-node hook in favor of the stock paths above. Operational details and the exact trust statement live in `op-supernode/silhouette/docs/RUNNING-V1.md` and `TRUST-MODEL.md`.

topPRs.title: op-private-interop!: establish the private-chain PoC reference
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Establishes an upstream draft reference for the private-chain interop PoC, including private execution, deterministic public projection, message-position resolution before publication, and persistent LightCL recovery. This is experimental work intended for eventual upstreaming after substantial review and refinement.

Projection spans are admitted as a whole before derivation releases their first new block. A pure Go/Kona validator enforces the transaction grammar, claim framing, per-block private OutputV0 records, and the span proof statement. After invalidation or sequencing-window expiry, publication binds to the canonical public parent and the last surviving private checkpoint, including a commitment to intervening replacement inputs. LightCL checks the local private output against the surviving record before adopting it, then retains its rewind, deposit-only replacement, and restart safeguards.

The verifier remains an explicitly configured insecure stub: publication is operator-attested, and private execution correspondence is not cryptographically verified. Protocol fallback blocks need no publisher proof; a future real proof must cover private execution through their recovery interval. This profile requires fresh deployments with interop and Isthmus active at genesis. Published spans cannot cross future activation blocks under the current rules. Initiating messages retain upstream's strict earlier-timestamp rule; same-timestamp dependencies remain unsupported. Private execution proofs, complete fault-proof execution support, and native ETH bridging/withdrawal settlement remain outside the supported profile.

Validation: targeted Go suites and repository Go lint pass; 662 affected Rust tests, strict clippy, no-std, feature propagation and SP1 guest lock checks pass; 31 private-profile Solidity tests plus three cross-language claim-vector tests pass. A fresh op-up private-interop smoke run passes. The full devstack/sysgo private-interop acceptance run passes all 13 enabled tests in 37m23s, including outage/expiry, invalidation, L1 reorgs, interrupted recovery, and restart after newer valid history. Changed registry artifacts and its interface pass scoped verification. Repository-wide contract tooling also encounters unchanged dispute-game interface mismatches and conflicting duplicate ZK-game build artifacts; those unrelated files are outside this update. The optional production-cadence soaks have not been repeated for this change. Two independent scoped reviews covered derivation parity, recovery, and public-source publication; broader production/security and full-feature reviews remain necessary.

Known existing CI issue: broad acceptance shards previously exposed the ordinary-follow finality guard rejecting stock EL-sync bootstrap snapshots whose follower finalized label is ahead of its source. That guard is unchanged by this update and remains an open issue for the recovery stack. Prior CI results do not establish that this revision is green.

This reference excludes atomic coordinator/shared-block builder work and local deployment artifacts. It does not update running devnet images.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** the new claim wire format, per-block output records, contract bytecode and private genesis-output configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases. Preserve the private recovery journal alongside the private execution database. Unsupported private native bridge routes must remain disabled.

topPRs.title: op-private-interop,contracts!: derive and recover a private ETH chain public projection
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
Private interop keeps application execution private while publishing the message history needed by the public interop set. One private-chain genesis produces a deterministic public projection, using standard span-batch transport and cross-chain dependency checks. This replaces #22729 and uses the existing `private-interop/devnet-readiness` branch unchanged at `9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2`.

Ordinary L1 deposits execute against private state. On the public projection, user deposits are included as successful no-ops with no minting, state changes, execution gas or logs; authenticated system deposits still execute. After sequencing-window expiry, interop invalidation or an L1 reorg, the private node returns to a surviving authenticated checkpoint and rebuilds canonical deposit-only intervals before publication resumes. Recovery ancestry persists across restarts, and batch publication waits for private reconciliation and an authorized batcher epoch.

The PoC remains operator-attested; execution-proof enforcement and private withdrawal settlement are future work. Native ETH bridge routes remain disabled in the private profile. The diff also includes the companion L1 event-certificate contracts, which are separate from the projection mechanism. Versioned bundle tooling, remote private-pair smoke, and deposit/recovery/reorg/rotation/cadence tests support devnet preparation.

**BREAKING CHANGE:** projection deposit execution, the claimed-follow RPC and recovery journal configuration require matching clients/contracts and fresh databases when migrating from earlier prototypes. Configure the persistent recovery path and ordinary projection rollup RPC as documented in [DEVNET.md](https://github.com/karlfloersch/optimism/blob/9f679db23ac12be10049766843495a03eb2993c2/op-private-interop/docs/DEVNET.md). Installing the custom native ETH bridge implementation requires explicit send/relay permissions.

Validation on this unchanged revision:

- Fourteen targeted Go test packages pass, covering private interop, batcher, claim-follow, chain container, driver, engine, sequencing, source client, smoke and devstack.
- Ten focused Rust projection/genesis tests and 78 targeted Solidity tests pass (Foundry lite profile). Main-workspace and SP1-guest Rust formatting pass.
- Full Go lint finds two existing issues: unchecked `big.Int.Uint64` in the position resolver and import ordering in the private interop preset. The fixes prepared locally are intentionally excluded to preserve this revision.
- Current upstream `develop` has three merge conflicts with this branch, in devstack configuration/signer setup. No upstream reconciliation is included.
- Full protocol/security review, full devnet acceptance and the production-cadence soak remain outstanding for this draft.

topPRs.title: feat: add private interop cleanroom implementation
topPRs.author: opsuperchain
topPRs.body:
## Summary

- add the private-interop private/rendering chain pair, contracts, deterministic rendering codec, builder, and claim-follow path
- integrate the pair with op-deployer, op-batcher, op-supernode, op-interop-filter, devstack, and op-up
- add private-pair-aware interop smoke coverage and a design document
- harden the implementation after adversarial review: structurally close deposits, bind rendering inputs and emitters, cap amplification, remove the separate operator key/premine, disable the stock ETH path, and make rendering execution fully zero-fee

## `op-up --private-interop` topology

```text
                         L1 EL + beacon node
                          ^              |
                          | batches      | derives
         +----------------+---+      +---v-----------------+
         |                    |      |                     |
   normal A batcher    private-interop batcher       shared supernode
         ^                    ^                      public view: {A, B-render}
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-node   B private op-node               |          |
         |                    |                         |          |
 A sequencer op-reth   B private op-reth         A verifier   B rendering
   public chain 901    private chain 902           op-reth       op-reth
                              ^                                     |
                              +------ `/902/claimed` ----------------+
```

- Chain A is an ordinary public OP chain with a stock batcher and proposer.
- Chain B has two different histories sharing chain ID 902: the sequenced, user-facing custom-gas-token private chain and a public, derived-only rendering with no sequencer or mempool.
- The private-interop batcher reads private B blocks, converts exported logs into claim/replay transactions, checks the rendering parent, and posts an ordinary channel to L1.
- The shared supernode derives and judges `{A, B-render}` using the stock message database and cross-safety logic. It has no private-chain access and does not know that B is a rendering.
- The only private-interop addition in the supernode is the `/902/claimed` follow endpoint. It reconstructs the committed private-B safe block reference from public rendering claims for the private op-node; it does not alter judging.
- Private B and rendering B are never P2P-peered: they deliberately have the same chain ID but different genesis hashes and block contents.
- `--smoke` runs `interopsmoke` in the same process so private receipt positions can be resolved to their canonical public rendering positions.

## Verification

- `go test ./op-batcher/batcher ./op-chain-ops/interopsmoke/... ./op-deployer/pkg/deployer/state ./op-interop-filter/filter ./op-private-interop/... ./op-supernode/supernode/chain_container -count=1`
- focused op-deployer private-interop genesis/rollup integration tests
- 49/49 private-interop Solidity tests
- 24/24 L2-to-L2 messenger Solidity tests
- 15/15 L2 genesis Solidity tests
- `op-up --private-interop --smoke`: chain identity, native transfers, valid messages in both directions, rendered private-chain message resolution, and invalid-message reorg all pass

## Notes

This is intentionally a draft for design and security review. The stock Superchain ETH bridge smoke case is skipped on the custom-gas-token private half; that path is closed by design and `NativeMintBridge` is the sanctioned liquidity path.

topPRs.title: private-interop: derive public projection from one genesis
topPRs.author: karlfloersch
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This carries forward the private interop implementation from #22720, but replaces the draft's two-role/two-deployer genesis flow with one source of truth:

- op-deployer emits one private-chain genesis and rollup config; there is no public/rendering deployer role
- `ProjectGenesisFrom(privateChainGenesis)` is a pure, deterministic local transform with independent Go and Rust implementations and a shared cross-language golden vector
- op-reth accepts the same private genesis and applies the projection before database initialization with `--rollup.private[=true]`; the private EL consumes it unchanged
- op-batcher and op-supernode detect `private_interop` from the private rollup config, load the local private genesis, and derive the public projection automatically
- the projected state restores stock ETH semantics, installs the replay/claim predeploys, removes private-only liquidity/mint machinery, and clears only the private-chain feature bit
- private interop derives an L1 resource configuration with `maxResourceLimit = 0`, closing deposits through the stock portal rather than a custom L1 contract
- old role flags, compatibility paths, configurable projection predeploy addresses, and the second op-deployer run are deleted

The remainder of #22720 is retained: claim/replay contracts and codec, deterministic batch construction, claim-follow routing, interop-filter integration, devstack/op-up wiring, and acceptance coverage.

## Deployment shape

1. Run op-deployer once with the chain's `privateInterop` stanza and custom gas token configuration.
2. Give the emitted genesis to the private op-reth normally.
3. Give that same genesis to the public-projection op-reth with `--rollup.private=true`.
4. Give the private genesis path to op-batcher and op-supernode; their private-interop paths activate from the rollup marker and derive the matching projection locally.
5. Give the private LightCL the ordinary private-chain genesis/config. It follows the supernode's `/claimed` route as in #22720.

No projection step performs a network call. The embedded implementation bytecode is checked against the current contracts artifacts in the op-deployer integration test.

## Verification

- `go test ./op-private-interop/...`
- `go test ./op-batcher/batcher ./op-batcher/flags`
- `go test ./op-supernode/cmd ./op-supernode/supernode/...`
- `go test ./op-interop-filter/... ./op-node/rollup`
- focused op-deployer private-interop integration, pipeline, and state tests
- `go test ./op-devstack/sysgo -run '^$'`
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-chainspec private_interop` (4/4)
- `cargo test -p reth-optimism-node private` (1/1)
- `just lint` in contracts-bedrock

The broad op-deployer pipeline package also ran locally; its only failures were nine live-Sepolia tests that require `SEPOLIA_RPC_URL`. The focused private-interop tests pass.

A manual deletion/configuration review was completed, including a differential comparison against the retired two-deployer genesis path. Automated sub-agent review was unavailable in this harness.
